name: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis

criteria.description: Histological identification of Langerhans cells in lesional tissue (characteristic morphology with grooved/folded nuclei)
Positive immunohistochemistry for CD1a and/or CD207 (langerin) on lesional cells
Birbeck granules on electron microscopy (pentalaminar rod-shaped or racket-shaped structures)
BRAF V600E mutation in lesional tissue (~50-60% of cases)
Compatible clinical and radiographic features (lytic bone lesions, skin rash, diabetes insipidus)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Definitive diagnosis requires biopsy with positive CD1a and/or langerin (CD207) staining. Presumptive diagnosis may be made with compatible clinical/imaging plus characteristic morphology.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Classified as single-system (SS) vs multi-system (MS), and risk organ involvement (liver, spleen, bone marrow). Now considered a neoplastic/clonal disorder of myeloid lineage, not purely inflammatory.

laboratory: CBC may show cytopenias if bone marrow involved
Liver function tests: elevated ALP, GGT if hepatic involvement
Urine specific gravity/osmolality: low if diabetes insipidus present
BRAF V600E mutation in lesional tissue (~55%) or cell-free DNA
imaging: Skeletal survey/X-rays: punched-out lytic bone lesions without sclerotic rim
CT chest: cysts and nodules in upper/middle lung zones (pulmonary LCH)
MRI brain/pituitary: pituitary stalk thickening, loss of posterior pituitary bright spot
PET-CT: FDG-avid bone and soft tissue lesions; useful for staging and response assessment
other: Biopsy with CD1a and langerin (CD207) immunohistochemistry: diagnostic gold standard
Electron microscopy: Birbeck granules (tennis-racket shaped; pathognomonic but not required)
Water deprivation test for suspected diabetes insipidus
Pulmonary function tests in pulmonary LCH

distinguishingFeatures: ECD has bilateral symmetric osteosclerosis of long bone diaphyses
Both may have BRAF V600E mutations
Ewing sarcoma has onion-skin periosteal reaction
Ewing shows small round blue cell tumor on biopsy
Different imaging pattern with periosteal reaction

redFlags: Risk organ involvement (liver, spleen, bone marrow) in children - requires urgent intensive chemotherapy
Diabetes insipidus (may be irreversible even with treatment)
CNS neurodegenerative changes (progressive, may not respond to chemotherapy)
Multi-system disease in infants (historically high mortality)
references: Allen CE, et al. Langerhans-cell histiocytosis. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(9):856-868.
Rodriguez-Galindo C, Allen CE. Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Blood. 2020;135(16):1319-1331.
Badalian-Very G, et al. Recurrent BRAF mutations in Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Blood. 2010;116(11):1919-1923.
